files.lesson.md: --- order: 35 unit: models9 node: AC9M9M05 n2 uses: [AC9M9M05 n1] assumes: [AC9M9M05 n1] connection: bushwalk-time title: Solve the rate model summary: "Use the model backwards and forwards: from the walk to the time, and from the time you have to the distance you can cover. Say what the answer means for the plan." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The walk takes about 3 hours by the rule. When do we need to leave to be back before dark?" --- Naismith's rule says about 5 km/h on level ground plus 1 hour for every 600 m of climb ([bushwalk.com navigation FAQ](https://faq.bushwalk.com/FAQ_Navigation.htm), checked 25 October 2026). The lookout track is 8 km with 450 m of climb, which takes 2.35 hours to walk up. The way back has no climb to count. When should the group leave so they are back by 4:30 pm? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. (The times are made up for the task.) ## Predict: the way back ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing the return time shows whether students double the whole walk, including the climb, or only the part that repeats." check: type: predict q: "Going up the lookout track (8 km, 450 m climb) takes 2.35 hours by the rule. About how long does walking back down take, with no climb to count?" options: - "1.6 hours" - "2.35 hours" - "4.7 hours" - "0.75 hours" actual: "1.6 hours. The way back is 8 km on a rule of 5 km/h, with no climb to add: 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 hours. Doubling the whole walk would give 4.7 hours, counting the climb twice." ``` ## Run: time from the model ```step stage: run insight: "The same model gives the return time: only the distance part is left." check: { type: number, q: "How long does the walk back take by the rule? (hours)", answer: 1.6, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 hours." } ``` ## Investigate: put the times together ```step stage: investigate insight: "The whole outing is the walk up, any stop, and the walk back. Work back from the finish to find the start." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Up takes $2.35$ hours and back takes $1.6$ hours. How long is the walk up and back? (hours)" answer: 3.95 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "2.35 + 1.6 = 3.95 hours." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $2.35 + 1.6$?", answer: 3.95, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "2.35 + 1.6 = 3.95." } - check: type: number q: "The group stops for $0.5$ hours at the lookout. How long is the whole outing? (hours)" answer: 4.45 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "3.95 + 0.5 = 4.45 hours." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ben" text: "Ben finds the time up and back. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: round-trip-double explain: "Line 3: the way back has no climb to count, so the climb is added once, not twice." ``` ### Up and back ```worked \text{up} = 8 \div 5 + 450 \div 600 = 2.35 :: Hours up. \text{back} = 8 \div 5 = 1.6 :: Hours back: no climb. \text{up and back} = 2.35 + 1.6 = 3.95 :: Walking only. 3.95 + 0.5 = 4.45 :: Add a 30 minute stop. \text{start} = 4{:}30 - 4{:}27 = 12{:}03 :: Work back from the finish. ``` ### Both ways ### Find the mistake Read Ben's working. Which line counts the climb twice? ## Modify: change the plan ```step stage: modify insight: "Using the model backwards: from the time you have to the distance you can cover." tasks: - hint: ["Take the climb's time away from 3 hours first.", "Then multiply by 5 km/h."] check: { type: number, q: "A group has $3$ hours to walk up a track with $600$ m of climb. How far along the track can they go, in km, by the rule?", answer: 10, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "The climb takes 1 hour, leaving 2 hours at 5 km/h: 10 km." } - hint: ["Convert 0.45 hours to minutes: × 60.", "4.45 hours is 4 hours and some minutes."] check: { type: number, q: "The outing takes $4.45$ hours. How many minutes is the $0.45$ of an hour?", answer: 27, tolerance: 0.5, explain: "0.45 × 60 = 27 minutes, so 4 hours 27 minutes." } - hint: ["Count back 4 hours 27 minutes from 4:30 pm.", "4:30 − 4:00 = 12:30, then take another 27 minutes."] check: { type: question, q: "The group must be back by 4:30 pm and the outing takes 4 hours 27 minutes. When must they leave by the rule?", options: ["About 12:03 pm", "About 8:57 pm", "About 4:27 pm", "About 9:03 am"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "That adds instead of subtracting.", "That is the length, not the start time.", "That is too early."], explain: "4:30 pm minus 4 hours 27 minutes is 12:03 pm: leave by midday to be safe." } ``` ### How far ### Hours to minutes ### When to leave ## Practise: use the model ```step stage: practise insight: "Solving the model for time and distance." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A track is 10 km with 300 m of climb. How many hours up by the rule?" answer: 2.5 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "10 ÷ 5 + 300 ÷ 600 = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5." - check: type: number q: "How many hours is the way back, with no climb? (hours)" answer: 2 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "10 ÷ 5 = 2." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $10 \\div 5$?", answer: 2, explain: "10 ÷ 5 = 2." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a walk is 5 km with 600 m of climb. How many hours up?" answer: 2 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "5 ÷ 5 + 600 ÷ 600 = 2." ``` ### Up ### Back ### Review ## Make: when to leave ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the lookout: put the model, the stop and the finish time together, and say what it means." tasks: - hint: ["Up 2.35, back 1.6, stop 0.5.", "Total, then subtract from 4:30 pm."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Up takes 2.35 hours and back takes 1.6 hours by the rule, with a 0.5 hour stop at the top. How many hours does the whole outing take? (made up for the task)" steps: - ["$2.35 + 1.6 = 3.95$", "walking"] - ["$3.95 + 0.5 = 4.45$", "add the stop"] - ["4.45 hours is about 4 hours 27 minutes", "convert 0.45 of an hour"] answer: "4.45" answerLabel: "Whole outing (hours)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["3.95", "That is the walking only. Add the stop."] - ["4.7", "That counts the climb twice."] criteria: - "I used the climb once." - "I added the stop." - "I gave the unit." explain: "4.45 hours, so to be back at 4:30 pm they should leave by about 12:03 pm." - check: type: question q: "Should the group plan to leave at 12:03 pm exactly?" options: ["No: the rule is an estimate, so leave earlier to allow for a slower pace", "Yes: the rule is exact", "Yes: it is always right", "No: they should leave later"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "It's an estimate.", "A rule of thumb isn't a guarantee.", "Later makes it worse."] explain: "The rule says 'about'. Adding extra time keeps the group safe." ``` ### Total time ### Leave when **Also used in** - **Travel and events.** Working back from an arrival time to when to set off. - **Cooking.** Working back from serving time to when to start. - **Next lesson.** Judging how much to trust the model. ```teacher summary: Students use the rate model for the return trip and for planning a start time (AC9M9M05, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can use the model for a return trip. - I can work back from a finish time. - I can say what the answer means for the plan. struggle: "Counting the climb twice. Ask: does the way back climb as well?" before: > Students need Set up a rate model. The one idea: a model answers the question you ask it. Use it forwards and backwards, then decide what it means. Hours to minutes: 0.45 hours is 27 minutes. Naismith's rule is a rule of thumb (bushwalk.com navigation FAQ, checked 25 October 2026). The track and times are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the whole outing in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student doubles the whole time. ask: Does the walk down climb? fix: "No: the climb is counted once." stretch: Plan a real local walk using the rule and a map. support: A printed timeline to fill in. leads: | Continues AC9M9M05 node 2. Where it leads: Judging the model. exit: q: 0.5 hours is how many minutes? a: "30." explain: > Use the model forwards to find a time, or backwards to find a distance or a start. Say what the answer means for the plan, and leave a margin. ```
